issues.legal_issue: Recurring royalty and dead-rent payments for mining raw materials are revenue expenditure when they relate to the materials obtained rather than to the acquisition of a mining asset.
material_facts: The assessee carried on a business manufacturing lime from limestone and paid a fixed annual amount to the Government while continuing to work the lime deposits.
The payment was treated as royalty and dead-rent under the arrangement, and no lump-sum payment for acquiring the mining right was settled or paid.
The assessee’s rights allowed it to enter the land, win limestone, and build some premises, but it could not remove other minerals and had to allow other mineral lessees access.
The payments related to the limestone to be obtained, and no evidence showed that any part of them was a premium referable to acquiring the mining lease.
issues.conclusion: The annual royalty and dead-rent payments were revenue expenditure and were allowable as deductions in computing business profits.
issues.legal_principle: The enduring-benefit test in British Insulated and Helsby Cables Ltd. v. Atherton is not universal: an enduring advantage does not by itself make expenditure capital, particularly where payments relate to raw materials obtained. The Court relied on Assam Bengal Cement Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax for the applicable tests, and distinguished Pingle Industries Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Abdul Kayoom v. Commissioner of Income-tax, which involved payments for acquiring enduring assets or rights not related to the quantity of material obtained. It also relied on H. R. Rorke Ltd. v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue, Ogden v. Medway Cinemas Ltd., and Allanza Company v. Bell. The governing distinction is whether the payment is for acquiring a capital asset or enduring advantage, or instead relates to raw material obtained in the business.

rule.if: tax_deduction_classification_case and recurring_mining_payments and payments_related_to_raw_material and not evidence_of_acquisition_premium

predicates.tax_deduction_classification_case: The case concerns whether expenditure incurred in a business is deductible as revenue expenditure or is capital expenditure.
predicates.recurring_mining_payments: The business operator made recurring payments for the right to work mineral deposits.
predicates.payments_related_to_raw_material: The payments related to the raw material obtained through the business activity.
predicates.evidence_of_acquisition_premium: Evidence showed that some part of the payments was a premium for acquiring the mining right or another capital asset.

issues.definition: When a business-deduction case involves recurring mining payments related to raw material obtained and no evidence that they include an acquisition premium, the payments are treated as revenue expenditure.
